chunks: It is narrated from Yāsīn al-Ḍarīr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, who said:
I said to the Shaykh, meaning Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام: Inform me about a man who claims a right against another man, but he has no evidence for what belongs to him.

He said: Then the oath is upon the one against whom the claim is made. If he swears, then the claimant has no right. And if he refers the oath back to the claimant, and he does not swear, then he has no right.

If the one from whom the right is sought has died, and evidence is established against him, then the oath is upon the claimant by Allah, other than Whom there is no god, that so-and-so has indeed died and that his right is indeed upon him. If he swears, otherwise he has no right.

Because we do not know; perhaps he had already paid him with evidence whose whereabouts we do not know, or without evidence before death. Therefore, because of that, the oath became binding upon him together with the evidence.

And if he makes the claim without evidence, then he has no right, because the one against whom the claim is made is not alive. If he had been alive, he would have been compelled to the oath, or the right, or to refer the oath back. Therefore, because of that, no right is established for him.

key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: legal evidence or proof supporting a claim
key_terms.ٱلْحَقَّ: the claimed right or due owed to someone
key_terms.ٱلْمَوْتِ: death, affecting how the claim is adjudicated
key_terms.ٱلْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ: the defendant, the one against whom the claim is made
key_terms.ٱلْمُدَّعِي: the claimant, the one asserting a right
key_terms.ٱلْيَمِينُ: the oath used in judicial procedure

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone claims a debt or right against a deceased person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains judicial rulings concerning claims of financial or legal rights when a claimant lacks proof, and especially when the defendant is deceased. It establishes that an oath may determine the ruling, and that in claims against the deceased, evidence must be joined with the claimant’s oath due to the possibility that the debt had already been discharged.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3343 - It is narrated from Yasin Al-Dareer, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah, who said:
I asked the Sheikh, meaning Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as), "Inform me about a man who claims a right against another man but has no evidence to prove his claim."

Imam (as) said: "The defendant must take an oath. If he swears, then the claimant has no right. However, if the defendant refers the oath back to the claimant and the claimant refuses to swear, then he has no right either.

If the person against whom the claim is made has died and evidence is presented against him, the claimant must take an oath by Allah (swt), there is no God but He (swt), that the deceased owed him the claimed right. If he swears, the claim is valid; otherwise, he has no right.
This is because we do not know-perhaps the deceased settled the debt through evidence unknown to us or without evidence before his death. Therefore, an oath along with the evidence is required.

If the claimant makes a claim without evidence, he has no right because the defendant is not alive. Had the defendant been alive, he would have been required to either take an oath, acknowledge the claim, or refer the oath back. Hence, no right is established for the claimant."
[chapter-CHAPTER 27 - CHAPTER ON THE JUDGMENT REGARDING TWO CLAIMANTS EACH PRESENTING EVIDENCE THAT THE RIGHT BELONGS TO THEM]
بَابُ حُكْمِ الْمُدَّعِيَيْنِ فِي حَقٍّ يُقِيمُ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا الْبَيِّنَةَ عَلَى أَنَّهُ لَهُ‌
